summary: Candidate b912101 makes a single, minimal, correctly-scoped CSS change: apps/web/src/styles/global.css:855-863 extends the existing `.legal-nav-pdf`/`.legal-nav-back` hide rule from `max-width: 480px` to `max-width: 600px`, matching the `.legal-grid` collapse breakpoint already at 600px (lines 843-853). This directly targets the reported defect — at 500px viewport, `.legal-grid` now fits (460px, confirmed by prior round) but `.row.gap-12.legal-nav-actions`/`.legal-nav-back` in the sticky header (LegalShell.tsx:36-60) were still visible and overflowing to x=534.53. Hiding them through 600px removes that overflow contributor for both /privacy and /terms, in both the hybrid and legacy designs, because LegalShell is the single shared implementation for both routes/designs (PrivacyPage.tsx, TermsPage.tsx both wrap it unconditionally; hybrid-surfaces.css has no override for these two classes, confirmed by grep). The footer card inside LegalShell (lines 293-325) duplicates PDF/Back with no media-query gating, so those actions remain reachable and keyboard-usable at every width, satisfying "footer actions remain available." The change does not touch the 500px browser assertion, routes, tests, billing, checkout copy, or scoring — diff stat is exactly 3 files (global.css + TESTING.md + HYBRID_UI_MIGRATION.md), confirmed via `git show --stat`. The docs updates accurately describe the change as source-level reasoning, explicitly do not claim a browser pass, and list the same pending verification items (500/601/1280, both themes, both designs) the owner asked for — no overclaiming found. Existing Week3-4 PR8 legal.test.tsx assertions are jsdom-only (no CSS media evaluation) and are unaffected. I attempted to independently run a dev server/Playwright to visually confirm, but Bash/PowerShell were denied by the permission mode in this session, so verification here is static/source-level only, same limitation the builder reported.
